title: Complements or Substitutes? Technology Adoption and the Demand for Clinical Care: Evidence from Automated Insulin Delivery
abstract: arXiv:2609.12976v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Whether medical technology reduces or increases demand for professional care is central to understanding its effects on healthcare utilization and costs. We study automated insulin delivery (AID) adoption among 1,608 adults with type 1 diabetes treated in four specialist clinics of the Italian National Health Service, 283 of whom adopt AID. Because adoption is clinically targeted and staggered, we combine risk-set coarsened exact matching with a staggered event-study design. Matching retains 181 adopters with comparable untreated controls. We further adjust for differential pre-adoption trends by extrapolating the untreated trajectory in event time. After adjustment, AID adoption is associated with greater routine outpatient engagement. translated_title: 互补还是替代？技术采用与临床护理需求：来自自动胰岛素输注的证据
translated_abstract: 医疗技术究竟是减少还是增加了对专业护理的需求，这是理解其对医疗利用和成本影响的核心问题。我们研究了意大利国家医疗服务体系四个专科诊所治疗的1,608名1型糖尿病成人患者中自动胰岛素输注（AID）的采用情况，其中283名患者采用了AID。由于技术采用具有临床针对性和分阶段实施的特点，我们将风险集粗化精确匹配与分阶段事件研究设计相结合。匹配后保留了181名采用者及其可比的未采用对照组。我们进一步通过外推未采用者在事件时间维度上的轨迹，来调整采用前趋势的差异。经过调整后，AID的采用与更高的常规门诊参与度相关。估计结果显示，相对于55.2%的就诊概率基线，采用后一个学期患者就诊糖尿病专科医生的概率提高16.3个百分点，四个学期后提高39.3个百分点。
tldr: 该研究发现自动胰岛素输注技术的采用是专业临床护理的互补品而非替代品，采用该技术后患者对糖尿病专科医生门诊的需求显著增加，就诊概率在四个学期后提高39.3个百分点。
en_tdlr: This study finds that automated insulin delivery adoption acts as a complement rather than a substitute for professional clinical care, with diabetologist visit probability increasing by 39.3 percentage points four semesters after adoption.
